record_title: Sharp Euclidean damping frontier for weighted Jacobi on 2×2 SPD systems
scientific_context: For weighted Jacobi T_omega=I-omega D^{-1}A on a real SPD system, Euclidean one-step nonexpansiveness has the exact matrix ceiling omega_E(A)=lambda_min(A^{-1}D+DA^{-1}). In dimension two, minimizing this ceiling over all SPD matrices of fixed spectral condition number kappa gives 1+1/kappa for kappa<=3 and (14kappa-kappa^2-1)/(8kappa) for kappa>=3. Standard Jacobi is universally Euclidean nonexpansive exactly through kappa=3+2sqrt(2), while at and above kappa=7+4sqrt(3) some 2x2 SPD systems admit no positive damping that is Euclidean nonexpansive, despite spectral convergence for sufficiently small damping.
limitations: Exact arithmetic, real SPD matrices, and simultaneous weighted Jacobi only. The exact fixed-matrix criterion is dimension-independent, but the condition-number-only sharp envelope and radical thresholds are proved only in dimension two. The claim concerns Euclidean one-step error norm, not energy norms, residual norms, floating-point stability, smoothing factors, multigrid efficiency, optimal asymptotic damping, or implementation performance. Complete theorem-level text of several broad historical monographs was not inspected end to end, leaving residual historical prior-coverage risk.

artifact_inventory.description: Deterministic NumPy verification of the fixed-matrix Euclidean safety ceiling, the sharp two-dimensional robust envelope, both radical thresholds, and a spectrally convergent example with unavoidable Euclidean one-step amplification.
Deterministic output of the numerical verification.
